trigger: Replacement returns HTTP 500, malformed JSON or times out on GET /api/tags after the original exits.
expected: An inconclusive observation retains pending and the lease.
actual: Readiness folds all three outcomes into OLLAMA_UNAVAILABLE. Status then reports reachable=false, so cleanup can commit verified released. Original nonce stop itself never posts to the replacement.
evidence: test_resource_cleanup.py:146 models only a healthy replacement. The archived native stdout even contains a real GET /api/tags 500 during startup, demonstrating that HTTP 500 can come from a live listener, not that this run falsely released.
proposed_correction: Give cleanup a dedicated observation with distinct confirmed absent, responding and indeterminate outcomes. Exercise HTTP errors through the production readiness/transport seam.

trigger: A sent lease survives a daemon generation change, or a retained lease has no native owner and an external ready service is present when Start is requested.
expected: Reject an unbound retained lease and keep lifecycle operations from authorizing release on another generation.
actual: A tuple of job ID and telemetry carries no original nonce/PID/birth. Any currently managed native handle plus a usable baseline qualifies to stop it and clear that tuple. Without a handle the cleanup endpoint blocks a loaded target, but runtime.start can return a ready external status and the default runtime_control tail can call provider.release, which can POST keep_alive=0. This latter mutation is on Start, not on the cleanup POST.
evidence: test_resource_cleanup.py:107 removes native entirely; :132 gives an arbitrary tuple to the current native and expects success. runtime.py:107–113; provider.py:350–354.
proposed_correction: Bind leases at acquisition to the original generation or refuse reconciliation. Guard all lifecycle entry points before any release or spawn, including retained leases with no proven owner.

trigger: One row contains the exact name, digest and integer size_vram but omits model.
expected: Require the complete identity specified in correction-01/decision.md before stopping.
actual: row.get('model', row['name']) synthesizes agreement. Whitespace, conflicting fields, duplicates, invalid digest and malformed sizes are otherwise rejected.
evidence: test_resource_cleanup.py:94–103 covers conflicts and malformed rows but omits this single-field omission.
proposed_correction: Require model to exist and equal name; add a missing-model case with the remaining fields valid.

trigger: Final status fails or a pending cleanup began with no lease and a healthy replacement can run jobs.
expected: After a mutation keep recovery and prevent new model work until all evidence is known.
actual: A thrown status error, failed GPU bound and mismatched native exit preserve pending. The synchronous commit follows the three samples and snapshot. A disguised observation failure can still clear it (1). Pending guards start/reset/stop, but /jobs/analyze checks provider readiness only. With no lease, an empty replacement inventory and admissible telemetry can allow acquire/inference while reconciliation is pending. can_start can also advertise true during pending.
proposed_correction: Carry pending into readiness/actions and job admission; reject before scheduling/acquiring a new lease and test a pending cleanup without a lease.

trigger: The correct 0700 root and marker exist but its data child already resolves outside it. Alternatively the launched executable and hashed executable differ.
expected: Before product import or start, bind actual destinations and executables and claim the run once.
actual: Authority, grant hash, active DB row, expiry, frozen hashes and exclusive claim are checked. data_root is compared lexically; an existing symlink inside the right root is accepted and data/media or runtime writes can follow it. Tool hashes validate the binding file entries; actual sys.executable, child.chromium_executable, hardcoded Ollama and PATH-resolved telemetry are not compared by the validator. No recursive removal in v2. The real sealed child allows one maintenance click and at most one original-service stop.
evidence: test_cleanup_validation_harness.py validates replacement of the private root, not its data child. Audited historical tool paths and hashes agree. No out-of-root write observed.
proposed_correction: Create/validate a fresh owned nonsymlink data directory and perform safe relative opens for outputs; compare resolved tools actually used to the sealed bindings. Include authority/helper and runtime dependencies in the trusted launch manifest.

trigger: runtime.start raises after creating a native owner, or native-final.json cannot be written after cleanup.
expected: Preserve the original identity and write terminal evidence for every claimed run, even if ancillary proof archival fails.
actual: Separate bounded cleanup steps are an improvement. native is assigned only after start returns; native=None is treated as exited, so a failed start followed by close can settle without harness PID/birth/nonce evidence. proof(native) and native-final writes sit outside the budget and receipt protection. A per-file OSError can skip both even when receipt.json remains writable. Non-object owner JSON can raise AttributeError in proof.
evidence: Both archived run receipts and native-final agree on normal completion. The sealed test files do not exercise these finally paths.
proposed_correction: Capture identity as soon as the handle exists, distinguish never spawned from identity unknown, and isolate proof collection/archival from an outer terminal receipt and reservation finalizer.

trigger: Ledger returns unexpected nonzero calls with otherwise known closure, or ledger read fails.
expected: Record the actual debit or explicitly unknown count; reject a violated zero-model budget.
actual: Normal zero counts are read from SQLite and settled correctly. For nonzero actual the code retains reservation but leaves known and PASS_FIXTURE_ONLY/observation status intact, so it can return zero. On a failed ledger read model_actions retains its initial zero even though the count is unknown. Sealed zero-cap DB prevents ordinary debit; these are reconciliation/error-handling paths.
evidence: Both independently read DB rows show active=0 and calls=0; authority.settle checks row count and elapsed budget at tools/local_program_authority.py:244–261.
proposed_correction: Initialize count as unknown, require actual==0 and successful settlement for success, and record any failed attempt to retain a reservation.

trigger: Runtime observation fails or malformed inventory prevents later observations. Empty external service has no lease.
expected: Return accurate runtime/telemetry observations with a specific reason for each missing value, and clearly refuse external service.
actual: Responses now carry all fields. sample errors and deadline have codes. Broad catch maps transport/proof/inventory/status faults to RESOURCE_RELEASE_PENDING, then labels skipped runtime/after observations with the same code. In production readiness an HTTP error can become a successful runtime observation (1). Empty external inventory reaches verified noop before ownership check and final runtime showing external does not revise verdict.
evidence: test_resource_cleanup.py:235,260; real-zero-model-01/cleanup-response.json shows populated observations for owned empty inventory. Fixture checks do not exercise empty external service.
proposed_correction: Track the failed observation and distinguish skipped, unavailable and failed-with-cause. Check external ownership before classifying noop; retain valid empty owned noop.

trigger: A 409 cleanup failure is followed by a failed and then successful status refresh.
expected: Keep original cleanup cause, show a separate refresh error and clear it on successful refresh.
actual: Separate state and renderer preserve RESOURCE_BUSY. Non-envelope HTTP errors preserve status; plain 404 has ENDPOINT_NOT_FOUND fallback.
evidence: ui-fixture-01 receipt and harness lines 199–211 assert both transitions; check-03 TAP includes HTTP404 case.
proposed_correction: No correction required for the prior finding.

trigger: Reconcile ACK and executed harness after candidate rebuild.
expected: Match executed source and preserve historical discrepancy.
actual: All 47 sealed entries match both source commits and all 22 entries in each live child match the candidate. Old validation-02 hash remains historical. Dist asset changes are confined to the candidate build output among executable source inputs compared here.
evidence: audit.json, root_ack and live.*.frozen; controller intent matches both live requests.
proposed_correction: No change to old records; retain separate source and distribution bindings.

trigger: Loopback peer with malicious Host, or remote peer with loopback Host.
actual: In-process ASGITransport explicitly sets client and host for both production-guard cases. Each requires HTTP 403 ORIGIN_FORBIDDEN and zero stop calls. Header, Origin and extra input negatives also ran.
evidence: Independent cpu/stdout.log and frozen tests named in request.json.

trigger: Read an individual check reporting a simulated resource release.
expected: Label simulated inventory/handle proof and scope the terminal verdict.
actual: The simulated release check explicitly says fixture original-handle cleanup and receipt says PASS_FIXTURE_ONLY. Real report says zero-model observation and returns noop.
evidence: Both archived receipts, API responses, screenshots and matching harness hash.

trigger: Runtime lock already held on entry to cleanup.
expected: Include waiting for this lock in the same total action timeout and release controller busy state.
actual: 43-second cooperative timeout encloses lock acquisition, stop, sampling and status. A held lock test with shortened timeout asserts unknown, reason and released busy flag.
evidence: test_resource_cleanup.py:260–273 and independent cpu/receipt.json. The 90-second process controller is a separate bound.
proposed_correction: No correction required for the prior lock-wait finding.
